questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा परिवर्तनीय ऑक्सीकरण अवस्थाएँ नहीं दर्शाता है ?
questions.text_english: Which of the following does not show variable oxidation states?
questions.solution: Sc (Scandium) does not show variable oxidation states. Its electronic configuration is [Ar] 3d1 4s2, and it loses all three electrons to form Sc3+ as its only stable oxidation state. Fe shows +2 and +3, Cu shows +1 and +2, and Mn shows multiple states from +2 to +7. Therefore option D is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: Sc (स्कैंडियम) परिवर्तनीय ऑक्सीकरण अवस्थाएँ नहीं दर्शाता। इसका इलेक्ट्रॉनिक विन्यास [Ar] 3d1 4s2 है और यह केवल Sc3+ बनाता है। Fe, Cu और Mn सभी परिवर्तनीय ऑक्सीकरण अवस्थाएँ दर्शाते हैं।
questions.chapter: The d and f Block Elements
questions.topic: Variable Oxidation States of Transition Metals

questions.text: संकुल [CoCl2(en)2]+ द्वारा दर्शाई समावयवता का प्रकार है :
questions.text_english: The type of isomerism shown by the complex [CoCl2(en)2]+ is:
questions.solution: The complex [CoCl2(en)2]+ shows geometrical isomerism. It is an octahedral complex where en (ethylenediamine) is a bidentate ligand. The two Cl ligands can be either on the same side (cis) or on opposite sides (trans) of the metal ion, giving rise to cis and trans isomers. This is geometrical isomerism. Linkage isomerism requires ambidentate ligands, ionisation isomerism requires exchangeable ions outside the coordination sphere, and coordination isomerism requires two different metal centres.
questions.solution_hindi: संकुल [CoCl2(en)2]+ ज्यामितीय समावयवता दर्शाता है। यह अष्टफलकीय संकुल है जिसमें en द्विदंतुर लिगंड है। दो Cl लिगंड या तो एक ही तरफ (cis) या विपरीत दिशा में (trans) हो सकते हैं।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से किसका प्रतिचुम्बकीय स्वभाव है ? [परमाणु क्रमांक : Co = 27]
questions.text_english: Which of the following is diamagnetic in nature? [Atomic number: Co = 27]

options.A: Co3+, प्रबल क्षेत्र लिगन्ड के साथ अष्टफलकीय संकुल
options.B: Co3+, दुर्बल क्षेत्र लिगन्ड के साथ अष्टफलकीय संकुल

options_english.A: Co3+, octahedral complex with strong field ligand
options_english.B: Co3+, octahedral complex with weak field ligand
options_english.C: Co3+, in a square planar complex

questions.solution: Co has atomic number 27 with configuration [Ar] 3d7 4s2. Co3+ has configuration [Ar] 3d6. In an octahedral complex with a strong field ligand, the crystal field splitting energy (Delta_o) is greater than the pairing energy (P), so all 6 electrons pair up in the t2g level giving the configuration t2g6 eg0. This results in zero unpaired electrons, making the complex diamagnetic. With weak field ligands or in tetrahedral geometry, electrons remain unpaired giving paramagnetic behaviour.
questions.solution_hindi: Co3+ का इलेक्ट्रॉनिक विन्यास 3d6 है। प्रबल क्षेत्र लिगंड के साथ Delta_o > P होता है, अतः सभी 6 इलेक्ट्रॉन t2g स्तर में युग्मित हो जाते हैं (t2g6 eg0) और कोई अयुग्मित इलेक्ट्रॉन नहीं बचता। इसलिए यह प्रतिचुम्बकीय होता है।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित अभिक्रिया पर विचार कीजिए : 2-क्लोरोबेंजिल क्लोराइड + KCN → ? अभिक्रिया का मुख्य उत्पाद है :
questions.text_english: Consider the following reaction: A benzene ring bearing CH2-Cl group and Cl substituent reacted with KCN. The major product of the reaction is:

options.A: NC substituted benzene with CH2-CN and no Cl
options.B: NC substituted benzene with CH2-Cl and no Cl
options.D: Cl substituted benzene with CH2-CN and CN on ring

options_english.A: NC-substituted benzene with CH2-CN (both Cl replaced)
options_english.B: NC-substituted benzene with CH2-Cl (only ring Cl replaced)
options_english.C: Cl-substituted benzene with CH2-CN (only allylic Cl replaced)
options_english.D: Cl-substituted benzene with CH2-CN and CN also on ring

questions.solution: KCN is a nucleophile that preferentially attacks the more reactive benzylic carbon (CH2-Cl) through SN2 mechanism. The aryl C-Cl bond is much stronger and less susceptible to nucleophilic substitution under normal conditions because the lone pair on Cl is delocalised into the aromatic ring. Therefore, only the CH2-Cl group is replaced by CH2-CN while the ring Cl remains intact, giving the product shown in option C.
questions.solution_hindi: KCN नाभिकस्नेही के रूप में बेंजिलिक कार्बन (CH2-Cl) पर SN2 अभिक्रिया करता है। ऐरिल C-Cl बंध अधिक मजबूत होता है और सामान्य परिस्थितियों में नाभिकस्नेही प्रतिस्थापन नहीं देता। अतः केवल CH2-Cl, CH2-CN में परिवर्तित होता है और वलय का Cl अपरिवर्तित रहता है।
questions.topic: Nucleophilic Substitution Reactions, Reactivity of Aryl vs Alkyl Halides

questions.text: निम्नलिखित यौगिकों में से किसका pKa मान निम्नतम है ?
questions.text_english: Which one of the following compounds has the lowest pKa value?
questions.solution: A lower pKa value means higher acidity. 2,4,6-Trinitrophenol (picric acid) has three strongly electron-withdrawing nitro groups at ortho and para positions. These groups stabilise the phenoxide ion formed after loss of a proton through inductive and resonance effects, making it the strongest acid among the given options. p-Cresol has an electron-donating methyl group which decreases acidity. p-Nitrophenol and m-Nitrophenol have only one nitro group, which is less effective than three groups. Therefore 2,4,6-Trinitrophenol has the lowest pKa.
questions.solution_hindi: 2,4,6-ट्राइनाइट्रोफीनॉल (पिक्रिक अम्ल) में तीन -NO2 समूह हैं जो फिनॉक्साइड आयन को स्थायित्व देते हैं। अतः यह सर्वाधिक अम्लीय है और इसका pKa सबसे कम है।

questions.text: (CH3)2CH–O–CH3 को जब HI के साथ अभिकृत किया जाता है तो देता है :
questions.text_english: (CH3)2CH–O–CH3 when treated with HI gives:
questions.solution: When an unsymmetrical ether is treated with HI, the iodide ion (nucleophile) attacks the more substituted (secondary) carbon via SN2 mechanism or via SN1 if a stable carbocation forms. Here, I- attacks the secondary carbon (isopropyl side) because it is more susceptible to nucleophilic attack than the methyl carbon due to the formation of a more stable secondary carbocation. This gives (CH3)2CH–I and CH3OH. Option A is correct. Option B is incorrect because I- preferentially attacks the more substituted carbon, not the less substituted methyl carbon.
questions.solution_hindi: असममित ईथर के HI के साथ अभिक्रिया में I- नाभिकस्नेही अधिक प्रतिस्थापित (द्वितीयक) कार्बन पर आक्रमण करता है। इससे (CH3)2CH–I और CH3OH प्राप्त होते हैं।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित यौगिकों में से कौन-सा बेन्ज़ीन सल्फोनिल क्लोराइड के साथ अभिक्रिया करके क्षार-विलेय अवक्षेप निर्मित करता है ?
questions.text_english: Which of the following compounds on treatment with benzene sulphonyl chloride forms an alkali-soluble precipitate?
questions.solution: This question is based on the Hinsberg test. Primary amines react with benzene sulphonyl chloride to form a sulphonamide that has an acidic N-H hydrogen, which dissolves in alkali (NaOH). Secondary amines form sulphonamides that are insoluble in alkali. Tertiary amines do not react with benzene sulphonyl chloride. CH3CONH2 is an amide, not an amine. (CH3)3N is a tertiary amine (no reaction). (CH3)2NH is a secondary amine (alkali-insoluble precipitate). CH3CH2NH2 is a primary amine and forms an alkali-soluble precipitate. Therefore option D is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: हिन्सबर्ग परीक्षण में प्राथमिक ऐमीन (CH3CH2NH2) बेन्ज़ीन सल्फोनिल क्लोराइड के साथ सल्फोनैमाइड बनाती है जो क्षार में विलेय होता है। अतः विकल्प D सही है।

questions.text: जलीय माध्यम में CH3NH2 (I), (CH3)2NH (II), (CH3)3N (III) और C6H5NH2 (IV) की क्षारकता का बढ़ता हुआ क्रम है :
questions.text_english: The order of increasing basicities of CH3NH2 (I), (CH3)2NH (II), (CH3)3N (III) and C6H5NH2 (IV) in aqueous media is:
questions.solution: In aqueous medium, aniline (C6H5NH2) is the least basic because the lone pair on nitrogen is delocalised into the benzene ring, making it less available for protonation. Among aliphatic amines in aqueous solution, the basicity order is: dimethylamine > methylamine > trimethylamine. This is because in aqueous medium, solvation (hydration) of the ammonium ion plays a major role. Trimethylamine has three bulky methyl groups that hinder solvation of (CH3)3NH+, reducing its basicity. Therefore the increasing order is IV < III < I < II.
questions.solution_hindi: जलीय माध्यम में ऐनिलीन सबसे कम क्षारीय है (lone pair बेन्ज़ीन वलय में विस्थानित)। वसीय ऐमीनों में जलयोजन प्रभाव के कारण: (CH3)2NH > CH3NH2 > (CH3)3N। अतः बढ़ता क्रम: IV < III < I < II।

questions.text: रक्त का थक्का जमने में महत्त्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाने वाला विटामिन है :
questions.text_english: The vitamin which plays an important role in coagulating blood is:
questions.solution: Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting (coagulation). It is required for the synthesis of prothrombin and other clotting factors in the liver. Deficiency of Vitamin K leads to delayed blood clotting. Vitamin A is needed for vision, Vitamin E is an antioxidant, and Vitamin D is required for calcium absorption and bone health.
questions.solution_hindi: विटामिन K रक्त का थक्का जमाने में महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाता है। यह यकृत में प्रोथ्रोम्बिन और अन्य क्लॉटिंग कारकों के संश्लेषण के लिए आवश्यक है।

questions.text: जब कोई उत्प्रेरक रासायनिक अभिक्रिया का वेग बढ़ाता है, तो वेग स्थिरांक (k) :
questions.text_english: When a catalyst increases the rate of a chemical reaction, then the rate constant (k):

options.D: अभिक्रिया कोटि पर आश्रित बढ़ सकता है अथवा घट सकता है

options_english.D: may increase or decrease depending on the order of the reaction

questions.solution: A catalyst increases the rate of a chemical reaction by providing an alternative pathway with a lower activation energy. Since the rate constant k is related to activation energy by the Arrhenius equation k = A·e^(-Ea/RT), a decrease in activation energy (Ea) leads to an increase in the rate constant k. Therefore, when a catalyst is added, the rate constant always increases regardless of the order of the reaction.
questions.solution_hindi: उत्प्रेरक सक्रियण ऊर्जा (Ea) को कम करके अभिक्रिया का वेग बढ़ाता है। आरहेनियस समीकरण k = A·e^(-Ea/RT) के अनुसार, Ea कम होने पर k का मान बढ़ता है।
questions.topic: Effect of Catalyst on Rate Constant

questions.text: किसी विलेय 'X' का 1% विलयन सूक्रोस (मोलर द्रव्यमान = 342 g mol⁻¹) के 6% विलयन के साथ समपरासारी है। विलेय 'X' का मोलर द्रव्यमान है :
questions.text_english: A 1% solution of solute 'X' is isotonic with a 6% solution of sucrose (molar mass = 342 g mol⁻¹). The molar mass of solute 'X' is:
questions.solution: For isotonic solutions, the osmotic pressure is equal, which means the molar concentrations (molarity) are equal. Concentration is proportional to (mass/molar mass) per unit volume. So: (w1/M1) = (w2/M2) for the same volume. Here w1 = 1 g, w2 = 6 g, M2 = 342 g/mol. Therefore M1 = (w1 × M2)/w2 = (1 × 342)/6 = 57 g mol⁻¹. The molar mass of solute X is 57 g mol⁻¹.
questions.solution_hindi: समपरासारी विलयनों के लिए परासरण दाब समान होता है, अर्थात् मोलरता समान होगी। w1/M1 = w2/M2 से, M1 = (1 × 342)/6 = 57 g mol⁻¹।

questions.text: जलीय NaCl के विद्युत-अपघटन के दौरान कैथोडिक अभिक्रिया है :
questions.text_english: During the electrolysis of aqueous NaCl, the cathodic reaction is:
questions.solution: At the cathode, reduction occurs. In aqueous NaCl solution, both Na⁺ ions and H2O molecules are present. The reduction potential of H2O (2H2O + 2e⁻ → H2 + 2OH⁻, E = -0.83 V) is more favourable than that of Na⁺ (Na⁺ + e⁻ → Na, E = -2.71 V). Therefore, water is preferentially reduced at the cathode to give H2 gas and OH⁻ ions, making the solution alkaline near the cathode.
questions.solution_hindi: कैथोड पर अपचयन होता है। Na⁺ और H2O में से, H2O का अपचयन विभव (-0.83 V) Na⁺ (-2.71 V) की तुलना में अधिक अनुकूल है। अतः H2O का अपचयन होता है।

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A): जल में एथिलीन ग्लाइकॉल मिलाने पर हिमांक कम हो जाता है।
कारण (R): जल के अणुओं के साथ हाइड्रोजन आबंध बनाने की क्षमता न होने के कारण एथिलीन ग्लाइकॉल जल में अविलेय है।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A): Addition of ethylene glycol to water lowers its freezing point.
Reason (R): Ethylene glycol is insoluble in water due to lack of its ability to form hydrogen bonds with water molecules.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) ग़लत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) ग़लत है, परन्तु कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: Assertion (A) is TRUE: ethylene glycol is added to water as an antifreeze agent; it lowers the freezing point of water due to the depression in freezing point (a colligative property). Reason (R) is FALSE: ethylene glycol is actually completely miscible with water because it has two -OH groups that readily form hydrogen bonds with water molecules. It is soluble, not insoluble, in water. Since A is true and R is false, the correct answer is option C.
questions.solution_hindi: अभिकथन सत्य है: एथिलीन ग्लाइकॉल हिमांक अवनमन करता है। परन्तु कारण असत्य है: एथिलीन ग्लाइकॉल में दो -OH समूह हैं जो जल के साथ हाइड्रोजन आबंध बनाते हैं, इसलिए यह जल में पूर्णतः विलेय है।
questions.topic: Depression in Freezing Point, Colligative Properties

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A): जटिल अभिक्रियाओं के लिए अभिक्रिया कोटि और आण्विकता सदैव एकसमान होती हैं।
कारण (R): कोटि प्रयोग द्वारा निर्धारित होती है तथा आण्विकता केवल प्राथमिक अभिक्रियाओं के लिए ही होती है।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A): Order of reaction and molecularity are always same for complex reactions.
Reason (R): Order is determined experimentally and molecularity is applicable only for elementary reactions.

options.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: Assertion (A) is FALSE: for complex (multi-step) reactions, order and molecularity are NOT always the same. Order is an experimental quantity and can be any number including fractions, while molecularity applies only to elementary steps. Reason (R) is TRUE: order is experimentally determined and molecularity is defined only for elementary reactions. Since A is false and R is true, the correct answer is option D.
questions.solution_hindi: अभिकथन असत्य है: जटिल अभिक्रियाओं में कोटि और आण्विकता समान नहीं होती। कारण सत्य है: कोटि प्रयोग द्वारा निर्धारित होती है और आण्विकता केवल प्राथमिक अभिक्रियाओं के लिए होती है। अतः उत्तर D है।

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A): डाइमेथिल ईथर की अपेक्षा एथेनॉल का क्वथनांक उच्चतर होता है।
कारण (R): एथेनॉल अणु परस्पर हाइड्रोजन आबंधन से सम्बद्ध होते हैं जबकि डाइमेथिल ईथर में यह संभव नहीं है।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A): The boiling point of ethanol is higher than that of dimethyl ether.
Reason (R): Ethanol molecules are associated through hydrogen bonding whereas in dimethyl ether, it is not possible.

options.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are TRUE, and R correctly explains A. Ethanol (boiling point 78.4°C) has a higher boiling point than dimethyl ether (boiling point -24.9°C) because ethanol molecules can form intermolecular hydrogen bonds through their -OH group (O-H...O type). This requires more energy to break, raising the boiling point. Dimethyl ether does not have an O-H group and cannot form such hydrogen bonds between its own molecules, hence it has a much lower boiling point.
questions.solution_hindi: दोनों सत्य हैं और कारण, अभिकथन की सही व्याख्या करता है। एथेनॉल में -OH समूह होता है जो अंतरआण्विक हाइड्रोजन आबंध बनाता है, जिससे इसका क्वथनांक उच्च होता है। डाइमेथिल ईथर में ऐसा हाइड्रोजन आबंध संभव नहीं।

अभिकथन (A): ऐनिलीन फ्रीडेल-क्राफ्ट्स अभिक्रिया नहीं करती है।
कारण (R): फ्रीडेल-क्राफ्ट्स अभिक्रिया एक इलेक्ट्रॉनरागी प्रतिस्थापन अभिक्रिया है।

Reason (R): Friedel-Crafts reaction is an electrophilic substitution reaction.

questions.solution: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are TRUE, but R does not correctly explain A. Assertion A is true: aniline does not undergo Friedel-Crafts reaction. Reason R is also true: Friedel-Crafts is indeed an electrophilic substitution. However, R does not explain why aniline fails to react. The real reason aniline doesn't undergo Friedel-Crafts reaction is that the amino group (-NH2) acts as a Lewis base and reacts with the Lewis acid catalyst (AlCl3) to form a salt (-NH2→AlCl3), deactivating both the catalyst and the ring. This is not explained by simply saying it is an electrophilic substitution.

अथवा

questions.text_english:
(a) Define molal depression constant. How is it related to enthalpy of fusion?
OR
(b) What type of deviation is shown by ethanol and acetone mixture? Give reason. What type of azeotropic mixture is formed by that deviation?

key_points: (a) Molal depression constant (Kf) is the depression in freezing point when 1 mole of solute is dissolved in 1 kg of solvent. Kf = (R × Tf² × M1)/(1000 × ΔfusH)
(b) Ethanol-acetone shows positive deviation from Raoult's law. Ethanol-acetone azeotrope is a minimum boiling azeotrope.

questions.solution:
(a) The molal depression constant (Kf or cryoscopic constant) is defined as the depression in the freezing point of a solvent when one mole of a non-volatile, non-electrolyte solute is dissolved in one kilogram (1000 g) of the solvent. It is related to the enthalpy of fusion by the formula: Kf = (R × Tf² × M1) / (1000 × ΔfusH), where R is the gas constant, Tf is the freezing point of pure solvent in kelvin, M1 is the molar mass of the solvent, and ΔfusH is the enthalpy of fusion of the solvent.

(b) Ethanol and acetone mixture shows positive deviation from Raoult's law. In pure ethanol, molecules are associated through hydrogen bonding. When acetone is added, ethanol-acetone interactions are weaker than ethanol-ethanol hydrogen bonds, so the escaping tendency of molecules increases and the vapour pressure becomes higher than ideal. This positive deviation forms a minimum boiling azeotrope.

questions.text_english:
(a) In a reaction, if the concentration of reactant 'X' is tripled, the rate of reaction becomes twenty-seven times. What is the order of the reaction?
(b) State a condition under which a bimolecular reaction is kinetically a first-order reaction. Give an example of such a reaction.

key_points: (a) Order = 3 (third order); Rate ∝ [X]^n; 27 = 3^n; n = 3
(b) When one reactant is present in large excess (pseudo-first order); example: hydrolysis of ethyl acetate CH3COOC2H5 + H2O → CH3COOH + C2H5OH

questions.solution:
(a) Rate = k[X]^n. When [X] is tripled, rate becomes 27 times. So 27 = 3^n, which gives n = 3. The order of the reaction is 3 (third order).

(b) A bimolecular reaction becomes kinetically a first-order reaction (pseudo-first order) when one of the reactants is present in large excess so that its concentration remains essentially constant throughout the reaction. For example, the acid-catalysed hydrolysis of ethyl acetate: CH3COOC2H5 + H2O → CH3COOH + C2H5OH. Here water is in large excess, so the rate depends only on the concentration of the ester, making it a pseudo-first order reaction.
questions.topic: Order of Reaction, Pseudo-First Order Reactions

(क) 2MnO4⁻ + 5SO3²⁻ + 6H⁺ →
(ख) Cr2O7²⁻ + 14H⁺ + 6Fe²⁺ →
questions.text_english:
Complete the following ionic equations:
(a) 2MnO4⁻ + 5SO3²⁻ + 6H⁺ →
(b) Cr2O7²⁻ + 14H⁺ + 6Fe²⁺ →

key_points: (a) 2MnO4⁻ + 5SO3²⁻ + 6H⁺ → 2Mn²⁺ + 5SO4²⁻ + 3H2O
(b) Cr2O7²⁻ + 14H⁺ + 6Fe²⁺ → 2Cr³⁺ + 6Fe³⁺ + 7H2O

questions.solution:
(a) 2MnO4⁻ + 5SO3²⁻ + 6H⁺ → 2Mn²⁺ + 5SO4²⁻ + 3H2O. In this reaction, permanganate (MnO4⁻) acts as an oxidising agent and is reduced from Mn(+7) to Mn²⁺(+2), while sulphite (SO3²⁻) is oxidised to sulphate (SO4²⁻).

(b) Cr2O7²⁻ + 14H⁺ + 6Fe²⁺ → 2Cr³⁺ + 6Fe³⁺ + 7H2O. Dichromate (Cr2O7²⁻) acts as an oxidising agent; Cr is reduced from +6 to +3, while Fe²⁺ is oxidised to Fe³⁺.

questions.text:
(क) निम्नलिखित युगल में से कौन-सा हैलोजन यौगिक SN2 अभिक्रियाओं में तीव्रता से अभिक्रिया करेगा और क्यों ?
CH3–CH2–I अथवा CH3–CH2–Br
(ख) क्लोरोफॉर्म बन्द गहरी रंगीन बोतलों में क्यों भंडारित किया जाता है ?
questions.text_english:
(a) Which halogen compound in the following pair will react faster in SN2 reactions and why?
CH3–CH2–I OR CH3–CH2–Br
(b) Why is chloroform stored in closed dark coloured bottles?

key_points: (a) CH3–CH2–I reacts faster; C–I bond is longer and weaker; iodine is a better leaving group
(b) Chloroform oxidises in air and light to form phosgene (COCl2), a toxic gas; dark bottles prevent this

questions.solution:
(a) CH3–CH2–I (iodoethane) reacts faster in SN2 reactions than CH3–CH2–Br (bromoethane). In SN2 reactions, the rate depends on the ease with which the leaving group departs. The C–I bond is longer and weaker compared to C–Br, and I⁻ is a better leaving group than Br⁻ because iodide ion is larger, more polarisable and more stable. Therefore iodoethane reacts faster.

(b) Chloroform (CHCl3) is stored in closed, dark-coloured bottles to prevent its oxidation. In the presence of air and light, chloroform gets oxidised to phosgene (COCl2), which is an extremely toxic gas. Dark bottles prevent light from initiating this photochemical oxidation, and airtight sealing prevents contact with oxygen.

questions.text:
निम्नलिखित के साथ ग्लूकोस की अभिक्रिया दीजिए :
(क) HCN
(ख) सान्द्र HNO3
questions.text_english:
Give reaction of glucose with the following:
(a) HCN
(b) Conc. HNO3

key_points: (a) Glucose + HCN → Glucocyanhydrin (cyanohydrin); the CN⁻ adds to the aldehyde carbon
(b) Glucose + Conc. HNO3 → Saccharic acid (glucaric acid); both -CHO and terminal -CH2OH oxidised to -COOH

questions.solution:
(a) Glucose reacts with HCN by nucleophilic addition. The CN⁻ ion attacks the electrophilic aldehyde carbon (C-1) of glucose to form glucocyanhydrin (a cyanohydrin). The product has an extra carbon with -OH and -CN groups: CH2OH-(CHOH)4-CH(OH)-CN.

(b) When glucose is treated with concentrated HNO3, it undergoes oxidation. Both the terminal aldehyde group (-CHO) and the terminal hydroxymethyl group (-CH2OH) are oxidised to carboxylic acid groups (-COOH), giving saccharic acid (glucaric acid): COOH-(CHOH)4-COOH.

questions.text: 200 g जल में किसी अवाष्पशील विलेय के 5 g को घोलकर विलयन बनाया गया। 300 K पर इसका वाष्प दाब 31.84 mm Hg है। विलेय का मोलर द्रव्यमान परिकलित कीजिए। (300 K पर शुद्ध जल का वाष्प दाब = 32 mm Hg)
questions.text_english: A solution is prepared by dissolving 5 g of a non-volatile solute in 200 g of water. It has a vapour pressure of 31.84 mm Hg at 300 K. Calculate the molar mass of the solute. (Vapour pressure of pure water at 300 K = 32 mm Hg)

key_points: Using Raoult's law: (P° - P)/P° = n2/(n1 + n2)
Moles of water n1 = 200/18 = 11.11
M2 = 5/0.0558 ≈ 89.6 g/mol (approximately 90 g/mol)

questions.solution:
Given: w2 = 5 g (solute), w1 = 200 g (water), M1 = 18 g/mol, P = 31.84 mm Hg, P° = 32 mm Hg.

Using Raoult's law for relative lowering of vapour pressure:
(P° - P)/P° = n2/(n1 + n2)
(32 - 31.84)/32 = n2/(n1 + n2)
0.16/32 = 0.005

n1 = 200/18 = 11.11 mol

0.005 = n2/(11.11 + n2)
0.005(11.11 + n2) = n2
0.05555 + 0.005 n2 = n2
0.05555 = 0.995 n2
n2 = 0.0558 mol

Molar mass of solute M2 = w2/n2 = 5/0.0558 ≈ 89.6 g mol⁻¹ ≈ 90 g mol⁻¹.
questions.topic: Relative Lowering of Vapour Pressure, Molar Mass Determination

questions.text:
0.2 M KCl विलयन की चालकता 2.48 × 10⁻² S cm⁻¹ है। इसकी मोलर चालकता और वियोजन मात्रा (α) परिकलित कीजिए।
दिया गया है: λ°K⁺ = 73.5 S cm² mol⁻¹, λ°Cl⁻ = 76.5 S cm² mol⁻¹
questions.text_english:
The conductivity of 0.2 M solution of KCl is 2.48 × 10⁻² S cm⁻¹. Calculate its molar conductivity and degree of dissociation (α).
Given: λ°K⁺ = 73.5 S cm² mol⁻¹, λ°Cl⁻ = 76.5 S cm² mol⁻¹

key_points: Λ°m(KCl) = 73.5 + 76.5 = 150 S cm² mol⁻¹

questions.solution:
Given: κ = 2.48 × 10⁻² S cm⁻¹, M = 0.2 mol/L.

Step 1 – Molar conductivity:
Λm = (κ × 1000)/M = (2.48 × 10⁻² × 1000)/0.2 = 24.8/0.2 = 124 S cm² mol⁻¹

Step 2 – Limiting molar conductivity:
Λ°m(KCl) = λ°K⁺ + λ°Cl⁻ = 73.5 + 76.5 = 150 S cm² mol⁻¹

Step 3 – Degree of dissociation:
α = Λm/Λ°m = 124/150 = 0.827

The molar conductivity of the KCl solution is 124 S cm² mol⁻¹ and the degree of dissociation is 0.827 (i.e., 82.7%).

questions.text:
एक प्रथम कोटि की अभिक्रिया को 25% पूर्ण होने में 40 मिनट लगते हैं। वेग स्थिरांक का मान परिकलित कीजिए। कितने समय में यह अभिक्रिया 80% पूर्ण होगी ?
[दिया गया है: log 2 = 0.30, log 3 = 0.48, log 4 = 0.60, log 5 = 0.69]
questions.text_english:
A first-order reaction is 25% complete in 40 minutes. Calculate the value of rate constant. In what time will the reaction be 80% complete?
[Given: log 2 = 0.30, log 3 = 0.48, log 4 = 0.60, log 5 = 0.69]
questions.solution:
For a first-order reaction: k = (2.303/t) × log([A]0/[A]t)

Step 1 – Find k: When 25% is complete, 75% remains. [A]0 = 100, [A]t = 75, t = 40 min.
k = (2.303/40) × log(100/75) = (2.303/40) × log(4/3) = (2.303/40) × (log 4 – log 3) = (2.303/40) × (0.60 – 0.48) = (2.303/40) × 0.12 = 6.91 × 10⁻³ min⁻¹.

Step 2 – Find t for 80% completion: 20% remains.
t = (2.303/k) × log(100/20) = (2.303/6.91 × 10⁻³) × log 5 = (2.303/6.91 × 10⁻³) × 0.69
t = (2.303 × 0.69)/(6.91 × 10⁻³) = 1.5891/6.91 × 10⁻³ ≈ 230 min.

The rate constant k ≈ 6.91 × 10⁻³ min⁻¹ and the reaction will be 80% complete in approximately 230 minutes.

questions.text:
(क) 2-ब्रोमोब्यूटेन के जल-अपघटन से (±)-ब्यूटेन-2-ऑल बनने में किस प्रकार की नाभिकरागी प्रतिस्थापन (SN1 अथवा SN2) होती है ? कारण दीजिए।
(ख) क्या होता है जब क्लोरोबेन्जीन और मेथिल क्लोराइड को शुष्क ईथर में सोडियम धातु के साथ अभिकृत किया जाता है ?
questions.text_english:
(a) What type of nucleophilic substitution (SN1 or SN2) occurs in the hydrolysis of 2-Bromobutane to form (±)-Butan-2-ol? Give reason.
(b) What happens when chlorobenzene and methyl chloride are treated with sodium metal in dry ether?

key_points: (a) SN1 mechanism; 2-bromobutane forms a secondary carbocation; water attacks from both sides giving racemic mixture (±)
(b) Wurtz-Fittig reaction; C6H5Cl + CH3Cl + 2Na → C6H5CH3 (toluene) + 2NaCl

questions.solution:
(a) The hydrolysis of 2-Bromobutane to give (±)-Butan-2-ol proceeds by the SN1 mechanism. The reason is that 2-bromobutane has a secondary carbon bearing the bromine. In the first step, the C–Br bond breaks to form a planar secondary carbocation (CH3CHCH2CH3)⁺. Since the carbocation is planar (sp2 hybridised), the nucleophile (water) can attack from either face with equal probability, producing a racemic mixture (equal amounts of R and S enantiomers), which is indicated by the (±) sign.

(b) When chlorobenzene and methyl chloride are treated with sodium metal in dry ether, a Wurtz-Fittig reaction occurs. The sodium reacts with both halides to form organosodium intermediates which then couple: C6H5Cl + CH3Cl + 2Na → C6H5–CH3 (toluene) + 2NaCl.

questions.text:
(क) निम्नलिखित अभिक्रियाओं में सम्मिलित समीकरण लिखिए :
(i) राइमर-टीमन अभिक्रिया
(ii) कोल्बे अभिक्रिया
(ख) फ़ीनॉल के ब्रोमीनन से 2,4,6-ट्राइब्रोमोफ़ीनॉल बनने में प्रयुक्त अभिकर्मक का नाम लिखिए।
questions.text_english:
(a) Write the equations of the reactions involved in the following:
(i) Reimer-Tiemann reaction
(ii) Kolbe's reaction
(b) Name the reagent used in the bromination of phenol to form 2,4,6-Tribromophenol.

key_points: (a)(i) Reimer-Tiemann: phenol + CHCl3 + NaOH → salicylaldehyde (2-hydroxybenzaldehyde)
(a)(ii) Kolbe's: sodium phenoxide + CO2 (under pressure, 400K) → sodium salicylate → salicylic acid on acidification
(b) Bromine water (Br2/H2O)

questions.solution:
(a)(i) Reimer-Tiemann reaction: When phenol is treated with chloroform (CHCl3) in the presence of aqueous sodium hydroxide (NaOH) and then acidified, an aldehyde group (-CHO) is introduced at the ortho position of the ring. The product is salicylaldehyde (2-hydroxybenzaldehyde). Reaction: C6H5OH + CHCl3 + 3NaOH → 2-HO-C6H4-CHO + 3NaCl + 2H2O.

(a)(ii) Kolbe's reaction: When sodium phenoxide (C6H5ONa) is heated with carbon dioxide (CO2) under high pressure (5–7 atm) at around 400 K, and the product is acidified, salicylic acid (2-hydroxybenzoic acid) is formed. Reaction: C6H5ONa + CO2 → (under pressure) → sodium salicylate → (H⁺) → C6H4(OH)COOH.

(b) The reagent used to brominate phenol to form 2,4,6-Tribromophenol is bromine water (Br2/H2O). The -OH group activates the ring so strongly that three bromine atoms substitute at ortho and para positions without needing a Lewis acid catalyst.
questions.topic: Reactions of Phenol: Reimer-Tiemann, Kolbe's, Bromination

questions.text:
आप निम्नलिखित रूपान्तरण किस प्रकार सम्पन्न करेंगे ? (कोई तीन)
(क) बेन्ज़ोइक अम्ल से बेन्ज़ैल्डिहाइड
(ख) ऐथेनैल से प्रोपेनोन
(ग) ऐसीटोफ़ीनोन से बेन्ज़ोइक अम्ल
(घ) ब्रोमोबेन्ज़ीन से 1-फ़ेनिलएथेनॉल
questions.text_english:
How will you bring about the following conversions? (any three)
(a) Benzoic acid to Benzaldehyde
(b) Ethanal to Propanone
(c) Acetophenone to Benzoic acid
(d) Bromobenzene to 1-Phenylethanol

key_points: (a) Benzoic acid → (SOCl2) → benzoyl chloride → (H2/Pd-BaSO4, Rosenmund) → benzaldehyde
(b) Ethanal → (HCN) → cyanohydrin → (H2O/H⁺) → lactic acid... OR ethanal → (CH3MgBr) → 2° alcohol → (oxidation) → propanone
(c) Acetophenone → (NaOBr, iodoform reaction) → benzoic acid
(d) Bromobenzene → (Mg/dry ether) → phenyl magnesium bromide → (CH3CHO) → adduct → (H2O/H⁺) → 1-phenylethanol

questions.solution:
(a) Benzoic acid to Benzaldehyde: Benzoic acid is first converted to benzoyl chloride by reacting with thionyl chloride (SOCl2). The benzoyl chloride is then subjected to Rosenmund reduction (H2/Pd-BaSO4, quinoline) to give benzaldehyde. C6H5COOH → (SOCl2) → C6H5COCl → (H2/Pd-BaSO4) → C6H5CHO.

(b) Ethanal to Propanone: Ethanal (CH3CHO) is treated with methylmagnesium bromide (CH3MgBr, a Grignard reagent) to give an adduct which on hydrolysis gives propan-2-ol. Propan-2-ol is then oxidised with acidified K2Cr2O7 to give propanone (acetone). CH3CHO + CH3MgBr → (H2O/H⁺) → (CH3)2CHOH → (K2Cr2O7/H⁺) → CH3COCH3.

(c) Acetophenone to Benzoic acid: Acetophenone (C6H5COCH3) undergoes the iodoform reaction when treated with I2 and NaOH (or NaOBr). The methyl ketone is converted to give benzoic acid and iodoform: C6H5COCH3 → (I2/NaOH) → C6H5COONa + CHI3 → (H⁺) → C6H5COOH.

(d) Bromobenzene to 1-Phenylethanol: Bromobenzene is converted to phenylmagnesium bromide (Grignard reagent) by reaction with Mg in dry ether. This is then treated with acetaldehyde (CH3CHO), and the adduct is hydrolysed with dilute acid to give 1-phenylethanol: C6H5Br → (Mg/ether) → C6H5MgBr → (CH3CHO) → (H2O/H⁺) → C6H5CH(OH)CH3.

questions.text:
निम्नलिखित अभिक्रियाओं में A, B और C की संरचनाएँ दीजिए :
(क) CH3CH2Cl → (KCN) → A → (LiAlH4) → B → (HNO2, 0°C) → C
(ख) नाइट्रोबेन्ज़ीन → (Fe/HCl) → A → (NaNO2 + HCl, 273 K) → B → (C6H5OH) → C
questions.text_english:
Give the structures of A, B and C in the following reactions:
(a) CH3CH2Cl → (KCN) → A → (LiAlH4) → B → (HNO2, 0°C) → C
(b) Nitrobenzene → (Fe/HCl) → A → (NaNO2 + HCl, 273 K) → B → (C6H5OH) → C

key_points: (a) A = CH3CH2CN (propionitrile), B = CH3CH2CH2NH2 (propylamine), C = CH3CH2CH2OH (propan-1-ol) + N2
(b) A = C6H5NH2 (aniline), B = C6H5N2⁺Cl⁻ (benzene diazonium chloride), C = C6H5-O-C6H5 (diphenyl ether)

questions.image_description: Two reaction sequences are shown. (a): CH3CH2Cl with KCN gives A; A with LiAlH4 gives B; B with HNO2 at 0°C gives C. (b): A nitrobenzene ring with Fe/HCl gives A; A with NaNO2+HCl at 273K gives B; B with C6H5OH gives C.
questions.solution:
(a) Step 1: CH3CH2Cl reacts with KCN (nucleophilic substitution) to give CH3CH2CN (propionitrile). So A = CH3CH2CN.
Step 2: CH3CH2CN is reduced by LiAlH4 to give CH3CH2CH2NH2 (propylamine). So B = CH3CH2CH2NH2.
Step 3: CH3CH2CH2NH2 (primary amine) reacts with HNO2 (NaNO2 + HCl) at 0°C. Primary aliphatic amines form unstable diazonium salts which immediately decompose to give the corresponding alcohol, so C = CH3CH2CH2OH (propan-1-ol) + N2 + HCl.

(b) Step 1: Nitrobenzene is reduced by Fe/HCl to give aniline (C6H5NH2). So A = C6H5NH2 (aniline).
Step 2: Aniline treated with NaNO2 + HCl at 273 K (0°C) forms benzene diazonium chloride. So B = C6H5N2⁺Cl⁻.
Step 3: Benzene diazonium chloride reacts with phenol (C6H5OH) in alkaline medium to give an azo compound (coupling reaction): C6H5N2⁺ + C6H5OH → C6H5-N=N-C6H4-OH (p-hydroxyazobenzene). So C = C6H5-N=N-C6H4OH.

questions.text:
संक्रमण तत्त्वों के स्वभाव के संदर्भ में (n-1)d इलेक्ट्रॉनों की भागीदारी इन तत्त्वों को कुछ विशिष्ट गुण प्रदान करती है। अत: परिवर्ती ऑक्सीकरण अवस्थाओं के अतिरिक्त संक्रमण धातुएँ अनुचुम्बकीय गुण और उत्प्रेरक गुण दर्शाती हैं तथा रंगीन आयन बनाने की प्रवृत्ति पाई जाती है। संक्रमण धातुएँ बहुत सी अधातुओं, जैसे ऑक्सीजन, नाइट्रोजन तथा हैलोजनों से अभिक्रिया करती हैं। KMnO4 और K2Cr2O7 इनके सामान्य उदाहरण हैं।
आंतरिक संक्रमण तत्त्वों की दो श्रेणियाँ लैन्थेनॉयड तथा एक्टिनॉयड आवर्त सारणी के f-ब्लॉक की रचना करती हैं। लैन्थेनॉयडों में 4f-कक्षक के इलेक्ट्रॉनों के अपूर्ण परिरक्षण प्रभाव (imperfect shielding effect) के कारण परमाणु क्रमांक में वृद्धि के साथ परमाणु आमाप में क्रमिक ह्रास होता है जिसके कारण आकुंचन होता है।
questions.text_english:
The involvement of (n-1)d electrons in the behaviour of transition elements impart certain distinct characteristics to these elements. Thus, in addition to variable oxidation states, they exhibit paramagnetic behaviour, catalytic properties and tendency for the formation of coloured ions. The transition metals react with a number of non-metals like oxygen, nitrogen and halogens. KMnO4 and K2Cr2O7 are common examples.

The two series of inner transition elements, lanthanoids and actinoids, constitute the f-block of the periodic table. In the lanthanoids, there is regular decrease in atomic size with increase in atomic number due to the imperfect shielding effect of 4f-orbital electrons which causes contraction.

key_points: Variable oxidation states allow them to form intermediate compounds with reactants
Large surface area (for metals) provides active sites for adsorption of reactants

sub_questions.solution: Transition metals and their compounds act as good catalysts because they possess variable oxidation states, which allow them to form intermediate compounds with reactants, facilitating the reaction. Additionally, transition metals have the ability to adsorb reacting species on their surfaces (large surface area provides active sites), thus increasing the local concentration of reactants and lowering the activation energy.

sub_questions.text_english: What is the cause of contraction in the atomic size of lanthanoids?

key_points: Imperfect (poor) shielding of 4f electrons; as atomic number increases, nuclear charge increases but shielding by 4f electrons is poor, so effective nuclear charge experienced by outer electrons increases, pulling them inward

sub_questions.solution: The contraction in atomic size of lanthanoids is caused by the imperfect shielding effect of 4f electrons. As the atomic number increases across the lanthanoid series, the nuclear charge increases but the 4f electrons shield each other very poorly because of their diffuse and penetrating nature. This results in a gradual increase in effective nuclear charge experienced by the outer electrons, which pulls them closer to the nucleus, causing a progressive decrease in atomic size known as lanthanoid contraction.

sub_questions.text_english:
Define lanthanoid contraction. How does it affect the atomic radii of the third transition series and the second transition series?
OR
In aqueous media, which is a stronger reducing agent — Cr²⁺ or Fe²⁺ and why?

key_points: Lanthanoid contraction: progressive decrease in atomic radii of lanthanoids from La to Lu due to poor shielding of 4f electrons
Effect: 3rd transition series (5d) elements have almost same atomic radii as 2nd transition series (4d) elements; pairs like Zr/Hf, Nb/Ta, Mo/W have similar sizes
OR: Cr²⁺ is a stronger reducing agent; E°(Cr³⁺/Cr²⁺) = -0.41 V shows greater tendency to lose electrons

sub_questions.solution:
Lanthanoid contraction is the steady and regular decrease in the atomic and ionic radii of the lanthanoid elements as the atomic number increases from La (lanthanum) to Lu (lutetium). It occurs due to the poor shielding of nuclear charge by the 4f electrons.

Effect on atomic radii: Due to lanthanoid contraction, the 5d (third transition series) elements are smaller than expected and have almost the same atomic radii as the corresponding 4d (second transition series) elements. For example, Zr and Hf, Nb and Ta, Mo and W have nearly identical atomic radii. This results in similar physical and chemical properties of these pairs.

OR (Alternative): Cr²⁺ is a stronger reducing agent than Fe²⁺ in aqueous medium. This is because the standard electrode potential E°(Cr³⁺/Cr²⁺) = -0.41 V is more negative than E°(Fe³⁺/Fe²⁺) = +0.77 V. A more negative reduction potential means Cr²⁺ has a greater tendency to lose electrons (get oxidised to Cr³⁺), making it a stronger reducing agent.

questions.text_english:
Proteins are the most abundant biomolecules of the living system. Proteins are the polymers of about twenty different α-amino acids which are linked by peptide bonds. Ten amino acids are called essential amino acids. In zwitter ionic form, amino acids show amphoteric behaviour as they react both with acids and bases.

On the basis of their molecular shape, proteins are classified into two types: Fibrous and Globular proteins. Structure and shape of proteins can be studied at four different levels i.e., primary, secondary, tertiary and quaternary, each level being more complex than the previous one. The secondary or tertiary structure of proteins get disturbed on change of pH or temperature and they are not able to perform their functions. This is called denaturation of proteins.

sub_questions.text: आवश्यक ऐमीनो अम्ल क्या होते हैं ?

key_points: Amino acids that cannot be synthesised by the human body and must be obtained through diet

sub_questions.solution: Essential amino acids are those amino acids that cannot be synthesised by the human body and must be supplied through diet. There are ten such essential amino acids (e.g., valine, leucine, isoleucine, lysine, threonine, methionine, tryptophan, phenylalanine, histidine, and arginine). Their deficiency in diet leads to health problems.

sub_questions.text_english: What is meant by zwitter ionic form of amino acids?

key_points: An internal salt form where the -NH2 group is protonated to -NH3⁺ and the -COOH group is deprotonated to -COO⁻; the molecule is overall neutral

sub_questions.solution: The zwitter ionic form of amino acids refers to the internal salt (dipolar ion) structure in which the amino group (-NH2) accepts a proton from the carboxyl group and gets converted to -NH3⁺, while the carboxyl group loses a proton to become -COO⁻. Thus the molecule carries both a positive and a negative charge but is electrically neutral overall: ⁺H3N-CHR-COO⁻. In this form, amino acids show amphoteric behaviour — they can react with both acids and bases.

sub_questions.text_english:
(i) Give one example each for Fibrous protein and Globular protein.
(ii) What type of linkages hold monomers of proteins together?
OR
(i) What is the structural feature which characterises a reducing sugar?
(ii) What is the structural difference between nucleoside and nucleotide?

key_points: (i) Fibrous: keratin (hair, nails) or collagen; Globular: insulin or haemoglobin
(ii) Peptide bonds (amide linkages, -CO-NH-) hold the monomers of proteins together
OR (i) Free aldehyde (-CHO) or ketone group (as in reducing sugars like glucose, maltose)
OR (ii) Nucleoside = sugar + nitrogenous base; Nucleotide = sugar + nitrogenous base + phosphate group

sub_questions.solution:
(i) Fibrous protein example: Keratin (found in hair, nails, wool). Globular protein example: Insulin (a hormone) or Haemoglobin.
(ii) The monomers of proteins (amino acids) are held together by peptide bonds. A peptide bond is an amide linkage (-CO-NH-) formed between the carboxyl group (-COOH) of one amino acid and the amino group (-NH2) of the next, with the elimination of a water molecule.

OR
(i) A reducing sugar is characterised by the presence of a free aldehyde (-CHO) group or a free ketone group (as a free hemiacetal/hemiketal in the ring form). This free carbonyl group can reduce Fehling's solution or Tollens' reagent. For example, glucose, fructose, and maltose are reducing sugars.
(ii) A nucleoside consists of a nitrogenous base (purine or pyrimidine) linked to a pentose sugar (ribose or deoxyribose) through an N-glycosidic bond. A nucleotide is a nucleoside with one or more phosphate groups esterified to the sugar. Thus nucleotide = nucleoside + phosphate group(s).

Fe(s) + Ag⁺(aq) ⇌ Fe²⁺(aq) + Ag(s)

questions.text_english:
(a)
(i) Calculate emf of the following cell at 25°C:
Zn(s) | Zn²⁺(0.001M) || Cd²⁺(0.1M) | Cd(s)
Given: E°Zn²⁺/Zn = -0.76 V, E°Cd²⁺/Cd = -0.40 V [log 10 = 1]
(ii) State Faraday's second law of electrolysis. How will the pH of aqueous NaCl solution be affected when it is electrolysed?
OR
(b)
(i) Calculate the ΔrG° and log Kc for the following cell reaction:
Fe(s) + Ag⁺(aq) ⇌ Fe²⁺(aq) + Ag(s)
Given: E°Fe²⁺/Fe = -0.44 V, E°Ag⁺/Ag = +0.80 V, 1F = 96500 C mol⁻¹
(ii) Write any two advantages of the fuel cells over primary and secondary batteries.
(iii) How many Faradays are required for the oxidation of 1 mole of H2O to O2?

key_points: (a)(ii) Faraday's second law: when the same quantity of electricity passes through different electrolytes, masses deposited are proportional to their equivalent masses; pH of NaCl solution increases (becomes alkaline) due to H2 and OH⁻ produced at cathode
(b)(ii) High efficiency, no pollution, continuous supply of energy as long as fuel is supplied
(b)(iii) 2H2O → O2 + 4H⁺ + 4e⁻; for 1 mol H2O: 2 Faradays

questions.solution:
(a)(i) E°cell = E°cathode - E°anode = E°(Cd²⁺/Cd) - E°(Zn²⁺/Zn) = (-0.40) - (-0.76) = +0.36 V.
Using Nernst equation: Ecell = E°cell - (0.0592/n) × log Q, where n = 2 and Q = [Zn²⁺]/[Cd²⁺] = 0.001/0.1 = 0.01.
Ecell = 0.36 - (0.0592/2) × log(0.01) = 0.36 - 0.0296 × (-2) = 0.36 + 0.0592 = 0.4192 V ≈ 0.42 V.

(a)(ii) Faraday's Second Law of Electrolysis: When the same quantity of electricity is passed through different electrolytic solutions connected in series, the masses of substances liberated at the electrodes are directly proportional to their equivalent masses (i.e., molar mass ÷ number of electrons transferred). When aqueous NaCl is electrolysed, H2O is reduced at the cathode (2H2O + 2e⁻ → H2 + 2OH⁻), producing OH⁻ ions. This increases the hydroxide ion concentration around the cathode, raising the pH (making the solution alkaline). At the anode, Cl⁻ is oxidised to Cl2, and the solution becomes slightly acidic near the anode. Overall, the pH of the solution near the cathode increases.

(b)(i) E°cell = E°cathode - E°anode = E°(Ag⁺/Ag) - E°(Fe²⁺/Fe) = (+0.80) - (-0.44) = +1.24 V.
n = 1 (one electron transferred per formula unit).
ΔrG° = -nFE°cell = -1 × 96500 × 1.24 = -119,660 J mol⁻¹ ≈ -119.66 kJ mol⁻¹.
log Kc = nE°cell/0.0592 = (1 × 1.24)/0.0592 = 20.95.

(b)(ii) Two advantages of fuel cells over primary and secondary batteries: (1) Fuel cells convert chemical energy directly into electrical energy with high efficiency (up to 70%) and do not produce pollutants — the product is only water in H2-O2 fuel cells. (2) Fuel cells can produce electricity continuously as long as fuel (e.g., hydrogen) and oxidant (oxygen) are supplied, unlike batteries which get discharged and need recharging or replacement.

(b)(iii) The half-reaction for oxidation of water is: 2H2O → O2 + 4H⁺ + 4e⁻. For 2 moles of H2O, 4 Faradays are needed. Therefore, for 1 mole of H2O, 2 Faradays are required.

(1) Acetophenone and Propiophenone
(2) Pentanal and Pentan-3-one
OR

(i) Give reasons for the following:
(1) In semicarbazide, only one -NH2 group is involved in the formation of semicarbazone.
(2) Acetaldehyde is more reactive than acetone towards addition of HCN.
(ii)(1) Arrange the following in decreasing order of their acidic strength:

(2) Name the reagent in the following reaction:
CH3-CH=CH-CH2-CN → CH3-CH=CH-CH2-CHO
(iii) Write the reaction involved in Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky reaction.

key_points: (a)(i)(1) Benzoic acid (C6H5COOH)
(a)(i)(2) Chalcone (PhCH=CH-CO-CH3), aldol condensation product
(a)(i)(3) m-Bromobenzoic acid (electrophilic substitution, -COOH is meta director)
(a)(ii)(1) Iodoform test: acetophenone (CH3CO-) gives positive iodoform; propiophenone does not
(a)(ii)(2) Tollens'/Fehling's: pentanal (aldehyde) gives positive test; pentan-3-one does not
(b)(i)(1) The -NH2 adjacent to C=O is less nucleophilic due to resonance; only the terminal -NH2 reacts
(b)(i)(2) Acetaldehyde has less steric hindrance and less +I effect than acetone
(b)(ii)(1) O2NCH2COOH > HCOOH > CH3COOH
(b)(ii)(2) DIBAL-H (Diisobutylaluminium hydride)
(b)(iii) RCH2COOH + Br2 + red P → RCHBrCOOH + HBr

questions.solution:
(a)(i)(1) Ethylbenzene when oxidised with KMnO4/KOH followed by acidification gives benzoic acid (C6H5COOH). The side chain is oxidised to -COOH regardless of its length.

(a)(i)(2) Benzaldehyde and acetone with dilute NaOH undergo a Claisen-Schmidt (cross-aldol) condensation. The product is benzalacetone (chalcone): C6H5CH=CH-CO-CH3 (4-phenylbut-3-en-2-one). Acetone acts as the nucleophile and benzaldehyde as the electrophile.

(a)(i)(3) Benzoic acid with Br2/FeBr3 undergoes electrophilic aromatic substitution. The -COOH group is a deactivating meta-director. The major product is m-bromobenzoic acid (3-bromobenzoic acid).

(a)(ii)(1) To distinguish acetophenone (C6H5COCH3) from propiophenone (C6H5COC2H5): perform the iodoform test with I2/NaOH. Acetophenone contains the CH3CO- group and gives a positive iodoform test (yellow precipitate of CHI3). Propiophenone does not have the methyl ketone (CH3CO-) group and gives no iodoform precipitate.

(a)(ii)(2) To distinguish pentanal (aldehyde) from pentan-3-one (ketone): use Tollens' reagent (ammoniacal silver nitrate). Pentanal reduces Tollens' reagent to give a silver mirror. Pentan-3-one does not react. Alternatively, Fehling's solution can be used — pentanal gives a red/brown precipitate, pentan-3-one does not.

(b)(i)(1) In semicarbazide (H2N-CO-NH-NH2), the -NH2 group adjacent to the carbonyl (the amide -NH2) is less nucleophilic because its lone pair is delocalised into the carbonyl group by resonance (NH2-CO- ↔ NH=C-O⁻). Only the terminal free -NH2 group (hydrazino -NH2) retains its nucleophilicity and reacts with the carbonyl compound to form the semicarbazone.

(b)(i)(2) Acetaldehyde (CH3CHO) is more reactive than acetone (CH3COCH3) towards HCN addition because: (i) acetaldehyde has less steric hindrance (only one methyl group) compared to acetone (two methyl groups), allowing the CN⁻ nucleophile to approach the carbonyl carbon more easily; and (ii) the two methyl groups in acetone exert more +I effect, increasing electron density on the carbonyl carbon and reducing its electrophilicity, thus making it less reactive.

(b)(ii)(1) Decreasing order of acidic strength: O2N-CH2-COOH > HCOOH > CH3COOH. The nitro group (-NO2) is strongly electron-withdrawing, which stabilises the carboxylate anion and increases acidity. Formic acid (HCOOH) is more acidic than acetic acid because the methyl group in acetic acid donates electrons (+I effect), destabilising the carboxylate anion.

(b)(ii)(2) The reaction CH3-CH=CH-CH2-CN → CH3-CH=CH-CH2-CHO is a partial reduction of a nitrile to an aldehyde. The reagent used is DIBAL-H (Diisobutylaluminium hydride), used at low temperature (-78°C).

(b)(iii) Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky (HVZ) reaction: A carboxylic acid containing at least one α-hydrogen is treated with Br2 in the presence of red phosphorus (P). The reaction proceeds through the acid bromide intermediate and results in α-bromination: RCH2COOH + Br2 (red P) → RCHBrCOOH + HBr. Example: CH3COOH + Br2 (P) → CH2BrCOOH + HBr.

sub_questions.text_english: Why is geometrical isomerism not possible in tetrahedral complexes having two different types of unidentate ligands coordinated with the central metal ion?

key_points: In a tetrahedral complex MA2B2, all positions are equivalent (any two positions are either adjacent or identical by symmetry); there is no cis-trans distinction

sub_questions.solution: Geometrical isomerism is not possible in tetrahedral complexes of the type MA2B2 (with two different unidentate ligands) because in a tetrahedron, all four vertices are equivalent to each other. Every ligand is adjacent (at the same angle, 109.5°) to all the other ligands. There is no distinction between 'cis' (same side) and 'trans' (opposite side) positions as in octahedral or square planar complexes. Therefore, no cis-trans isomers are possible.

key_points: [CoF6]³⁻ < [Co(NH3)6]³⁺ < [Co(CN)6]³⁻

sub_questions.solution: The crystal field splitting energy (Δo) depends on the nature of the ligand, arranged in the spectrochemical series. F⁻ is a weak field ligand, NH3 is an intermediate field ligand, and CN⁻ is the strongest field ligand. Therefore, the increasing order of Δo is: [CoF6]³⁻ < [Co(NH3)6]³⁺ < [Co(CN)6]³⁻.

sub_questions.text_english: Write the hybridization and magnetic character of the complex [Ni(CO)4] on the basis of valence bond theory. [Atomic No.: Ni = 28]

key_points: Ni configuration: [Ar] 3d8 4s2; Ni(0) in complex: 3d10 (all paired after CO pushes electrons); sp3 hybridisation; tetrahedral geometry; diamagnetic

sub_questions.solution: Ni has atomic number 28 with configuration [Ar] 3d8 4s2. In [Ni(CO)4], Ni is in zero oxidation state. Under the influence of CO (a strong field ligand), the 3d electrons pair up to give Ni(0) configuration as 3d10. The hybridisation of Ni in this complex is sp3, involving one 4s and three 4p orbitals. The geometry is tetrahedral. Since all 3d electrons are paired (3d10), the complex has no unpaired electrons and is diamagnetic.

sub_questions.text_english:
Out of [CoF6]³⁻ and [Co(C2O4)3]³⁻, which one complex is:
(i) more stable?
(ii) the high spin complex?

key_points: (i) [Co(C2O4)3]³⁻ is more stable (chelate effect of oxalate C2O4²⁻, a bidentate ligand)
(ii) [CoF6]³⁻ is the high spin complex (F⁻ is a weak field ligand)

sub_questions.solution:
(i) [Co(C2O4)3]³⁻ is more stable because C2O4²⁻ (oxalate) is a bidentate ligand that forms chelate rings with the metal ion. The chelate effect significantly increases the stability of the complex compared to [CoF6]³⁻, which contains monodentate F⁻ ligands.

(ii) [CoF6]³⁻ is the high spin complex because F⁻ is a weak field ligand and produces a small crystal field splitting energy (Δo < P, pairing energy). Therefore the 3d6 electrons of Co³⁺ remain unpaired as much as possible, giving a high spin configuration: t2g4 eg2 with 4 unpaired electrons.

sub_questions.text: उभयदन्ती लिगन्ड और द्विदंतुर लिगन्ड में क्या अंतर है ?
sub_questions.text_english: What is the difference between an ambidentate ligand and bidentate ligand?

key_points: Ambidentate: can donate from two different donor atoms but bonds through only one at a time (e.g., NO2⁻ or SCN⁻)
Bidentate: has two donor atoms and donates simultaneously through both forming a chelate ring (e.g., en, C2O4²⁻)

sub_questions.solution: An ambidentate ligand is one that has two different donor atoms but can coordinate to the metal ion through only one donor atom at a time. For example, NO2⁻ can coordinate through N (nitro, M-NO2) or through O (nitrito, M-ONO), and SCN⁻ can bond through S or N. A bidentate ligand is one that has two donor atoms which both coordinate simultaneously to the same metal ion, forming a five- or six-membered chelate ring. For example, ethylenediamine (en) uses both its N atoms to bind, and oxalate (C2O4²⁻) uses both its O atoms.

Write the electronic configuration of d⁵ in terms of t2g and eg in an octahedral field when:
(i) Δo > P, and (ii) Δo < P

key_points: (i) Δo > P (strong field, low spin): t2g5 eg0 — all 5 electrons in t2g, 1 unpaired
(ii) Δo < P (weak field, high spin): t2g3 eg2 — 5 unpaired electrons

sub_questions.solution:
For a d⁵ configuration in an octahedral field:

(i) When Δo > P (crystal field splitting energy is greater than pairing energy — strong field/low spin case): electrons prefer to pair up in the lower-energy t2g level rather than move to the higher eg level. Configuration: t2g5 eg0. There is 1 unpaired electron.

(ii) When Δo < P (crystal field splitting energy is less than pairing energy — weak field/high spin case): electrons prefer to occupy all available orbitals singly before pairing. Configuration: t2g3 eg2. There are 5 unpaired electrons (maximum spin).
